feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
entry.summary: The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct.

entry.title: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns following misconduct allegations
entry.summary: President Trump has forced out his ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle. She faced allegations of misconduct before and during her tenure at the U.S. Embassy in Athens, which she has denied.

entry.title: In Kansas, a newly competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
entry.summary: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.

entry.title: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to midterm polling places
entry.summary: For many election cycles, civil rights groups and political parties have fanned out to monitor polling places, but the charged midterm environment has many organizations stepping up efforts this year.

entry.title: Former White House ethics lawyer on Kimberly Guilfoyle's alleged ethics violations
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with former chief White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter about the ethics allegations facing former U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle, who resigned Tuesday.

entry.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle has been asked to resign among corruption allegations
entry.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle has been asked to resign as US ambassador to Greece following allegations that she sought payment from a Trump donor in exchange for access to administration officials

entry.title: Why does Pete Hegseth want to livestream an execution?
entry.summary: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has proposed livestreaming the execution of a man convicted of the 2009 attack on Fort Hood. Some scholars say the idea is rooted in his religious background.

entry.title: Conservative super-lawyer squares up for his latest Supreme Court argument
entry.summary: Paul Clement, a Republican, has racked up dozens of wins at the Supreme Court since his days as George W. Bush's solicitor general. Recently, he's been challenging some Trump administration policies.

entry.title: Bipartisan group of senators call on Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal
entry.summary: Six Democratic and six Republican senators wrote a letter calling on President Trump to withdraw from his recent deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

entry.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
entry.summary: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.
